ships.name: Legio
ships.description: The Legio is a light escort carrier, designed for the Navarchs' smaller fleets. Like its bigger sibling, the Regnum, it features Phase Torpedoes, allowing it to provide fire support from afar while its assigned fighter complement tangles up the enemy.

ships.name: Regnum
ships.description: The Navarchs specialize in sea-to-space ship designs, and the mighty Regnum is a premiere feature of that ideology. A massive carrier, modest in armament, but encased in ultra-heavy shields with a heavy duty hull. With its payload of 46 fighters on tap, it's an impressive ship by all measures.

ships.name: Regio
ships.description: The mighty Regio-class carrier is a sight to behold, either on the seas or among the stars. While it does show its age with a lack of Phase Torpedo tubes, refits over generations mean many of these ships use state-of-the-art shield and hull technologies, resulting in a ship that not only has a payload of nearly 100 fighters, but also is practically unkillable in the face of all but the largest of co-ordinated strikes.

ships.name: Epiregalimen
ships.description: The Epiregalimen started life as an attempt to update the design of the Regio-class carrier. Though the old design still served its role well, the hope was to "modernize" it, providing a more flexible platform from which to launch fighters. Perhaps ironically, the design's original intent was almost completely lost; the new carrier's lack of phase torpedoes, in particular, render it an antiquated-on-arrival design. Not that the Navarchs couldn't find a use for it, of course: It now serves comfortably as a heavy-hitter carrier in the largest Navarch fleets, delivering its nearly two-hundred fighters where needed with aplomb.

ships.name: Parvregalimen
ships.description: The Parvregalimen is a hybrid freighter-carrier, designed as a solo mining vessel in contrast to the cludgey nature of supplementing Regnum-class carriers with Imperiums. Though its payload isn't quite as large as a Regnum, the Parvregalimen has a very large amount of cargo space, allowing it to be a reliable drop-off point for mining fighters.

ships.name: Supravitae
ships.description: To command a Supravitae is the highest honor a Navarch can achieve; and serving aboard one isn't very far behind. The Supravitae has a more formidable armament than any other Navarch ship, and support for a whopping 76 fighters, putting it between the Regnum and Regio in terms of fighter payload. Also aboard are some more logistical facilities, such as a notably sized cargo bay, and a large amount of spare bunks for reserve crew or ground troops. 	Of course, the Supravitae is not an easy ship to build or obtain; purchasing one will almost certainly leave a significant dent in any captain's budget for a long time.

ships.name: Infrafamilia
ships.description: An "Outrigger" refers both to a secondary hull attached to a ship as well as the ship itself capable of accepting such attachments. The smallest of the Navarchs' outrigger vessels, the Infrafamilia by itself is the smallest, lightest ship in the Navarch fleet, effectively mimicking the role of a Shuttle. Despite this, it is still a full-sized warship, with a decent armament allowing it to tangle with other small vessels and fighters. 	Outriggers are an aging technology in Navarch space, largely held afloat by pre-existing supply and infrastructure. Though most planetary settlements lack the correct equipment to properly interchange outriggers; instead, loaded variants of the ship must be found aboard space stations, where the interchange infrastructure is much simpler and easier to run.

ships.name: Subsectio
ships.description: A larger Outrigger, dating back to the Navarchs' transition from versatile, modular outriggers to dedicated ship designs about 35,000 years ago. The design has seen some refits to keep up with the latest technology, but is only configurable at larger Navarch stations due to the unwieldly length of the ship mixed with its three outrigger attachment points. 	By itself, however, the Subsectio has its own merits, essentially being a lighter armed but more durable and nimble Ordo. As such, some Navarchs use the "empty" configuration as a light screening destroyer, at least until they can reliably afford the slightly more expensive (and far less durable) Ordo.

ships.name: Subforma
ships.description: The Subforma is a stealth combat drone developed by the Navarchs; effectively just a standardized cargo container converted into a compact, stackable drone, Subformae rely on their carrier to recharge their shields, insteady relying on their dense hull and newly-developed rearmoring tech to keep the drone functional. Subformae carry anti-capital weapons, allowing a swarm to quickly rip a large target apart should their carrier's on-board armament be insufficient.

ships.name: Forma
ships.description: Building on techniques learned during the construction of the Subvarietas, the Forma-class fighter is designed as a deployable anti-missile net, allowing any fleet to rapidly extend its field of missile denial. The design does have some drawbacks, however, such as the reduced engine capacity and hampered outfit space, meaning the ship is only used in its dedicated anti-missile role.

ships.name: Subvarietas
ships.description: With their fighters being deployed in such significant numbers with the expectation of casualties, the Navarchs invested heavily in advanced automaton designs. The resultant fighters, known as the Subvarietas, are practically miniature warships, able to soak up an absurd amount of damage while doling out both anti-capital and anti-fighter fire. 	It's actually quite impressive how highly engineered these ships are; armor is strategically placed around every outfit compartment, reducing both the space and mass the armor takes up while providing maximum protection.

ships.name: Tribus
ships.description: The Tribus is a minelaying destroyer used by the Navarchs to saturate a system in lathe mines; though one Tribus is already capable of outputting a significant quantity of mines, they Tribus' relatively small size and low cost means they are frequently fielded in sorties of 3 or more.

ships.name: Subfamilia
ships.description: Compared to its sister ship, the Subfamilia is specialized for long-ranged missile combat rather than minelaying. In addition to 10 launch bays for Ransacker Missile swarms, the ship features a Monolithic Anti-Missile as one of its "main guns", allowing it to sweep mines and block missiles from enormous distances as it bombards the opposition from long range.

ships.name: Genus
ships.description: With its heavy armament of Phase Torpedoes, the Genus is a fearsome ranged combatant capable of doing highly accurate damage over great range. Its role as a dreaded capital hunter has lead to a popular folktale about a sortie of Genera sinking an entire Quarg patrol before the Quarg's intrasystem scanners even had a lock on them.

ships.name: Supratribus
ships.description: The Supratribus is a focus-built artillery ship, designed to carry two gargantuan gauss cannons into battle, piercing through any amount of enemy ranks. By default, the two main cannons are the ship's only offensive weapon, so it requires support to be used effectively. As such, the Supratribus is only found among larger Navarch fleets.

ships.name: Familia
ships.description: A relic of an earlier age, the Familia-class missile cruiser has largely been supplanted by its smaller brother, the Subfamilia, in service. However, the Familia is still a long-ranged powerhouse, with its huge battery of Ransacker launchers and a pair of 7-62 batteries to shore up against more pinpoint targets. Additionally, the shield matrix is especially robust, adding noticeable amounts of durability (and weight) to an already difficult to hunt ship.

ships.name: Ordo
ships.description: The Ordo is a middleweight cruiser fielded by the Navarchs, designed to provide an effective anti-fighter platform while still retaining some long-range, anti-capital capability as well. To this end, it has only 3 main guns of reduced size, providing it with the ability to provide long-ranged support between fending off fighter sorties.

ships.name: Infracohors
ships.description: The Infracohors is a prototype "mini-battleship" designed as a testbed for the Navarchs' Shock Blaster turrets. The principle behind the design is that, by removing a need for barbettes, a ship can carry more armor and equipment in a similar space. The resultant ship is thus more mobile, tougher, and still capable of long-ranged attacks.

ships.name: Divisio
ships.description: The Divisio is a heavy battleship employed by the Navarchs, intended to be a capital ship counterpart to the Regnum. Armed more heavily than any human ship could dream of being, it Divisio is designed for both anti-capital and anti-fighter roles, with heavy anti-missile defenses to ensure it remains effective in the face of long-range bombardments.

ships.name: Phylum
ships.description: The Phylum is an experimental battleship featuring a number of new and exciting technologies by the Navarchs; most notably, their new beam weapon, the THEL. Armed for heavy anti-capital duty, the Phylum is a fearsome ship to engage, however a reduced amount of deck space compared to the tried and true Divisio means that the ships tend to fare well in different conditions, rather than one being overwhelmingly favourable compared to the other.

ships.name: Regalis
ships.description: The Regalis Super Battleship is a sight to behold. Featuring 6 barbettes carrying some of the largest turrets the Navarchs have ever designed, it is capable of annihilating most ships with a single blast from its main battery. However, the ship is also coated in anti-missile and anti-fighter turrets, with powerful Phase Torpedoes to strike distant foes. Perhaps expectedly, the ship's only major weakness is its speed.

ships.name: Infravitae
ships.description: Though its range for a Navarch capital ship is slightly piteous, the Infravitae is a monster of a vessel, capable of melting apart hulls with its array of twelve Tactical High-Energy Laser nodes. This, combined with improved engine systems and the upgraded hull all experimental Navarch vessels share, results in a beast of a warship, capable of blasting almost any other vessel out of the sky.

ships.name: Klados
ships.description: The Klados' design harkens back to the early days of the Quarg-Navarch war, when the Navarchs were looking for the fastest ways to amplify their fighting force. The Klados is a modular warship whose design, unfortunately, never got off the ground. However, the Navarch industrial sector is now far more robust, and some rekindled interest has led to an "explorative" reintroduction of the design. 	In its base configuration, the Klados stands out as one of the only Navarch light warships designed to "brawl" with other ships at short to medium range, rather than relying on missiles or other artillery-esque features to vex the foe from great range.

ships.name: Klados I
ships.description: This is the first of three "iterative configurations" on the Klados. This first model retains a good portion of its mobility while delivering far more bang to the battlefield, with twice the amount of capital turrets.

ships.name: Klados II
ships.description: The second iteration on the Klados features the most balanced performance, barely scraping into the heavy warship size bracket while remaining relatively light and mobile. Its range, however, leaves something to be desired.

ships.name: Klados III
ships.description: This is the first of three "iterative configurations" on the Klados. This first model retains a good portion of its mobility while delivering far more bang to the battlefield, with twice the amount of capital turrets.

ships.name: Nixus
ships.description: The Nixus serves the role of a lightweight refuelling ship in Navarch fleets, capable of swiftly darting around a fleet to refuel ships in need while also providing a consistent source of fuel for long journeys. The ship also wields a pair of Phase Torpedo tubes, allowing it to pelt enemies from a distance during combat.

ships.name: Subclassis
ships.description: The Subclassis is designed as an all-in-one auxiliary ship for Navarch military fleets; it carries a large amount of passengers, cargo, and fuel as part of standard operations, though its armament leaves much to be desired compared to similarly sized warships like the Ordo.

ships.name: Microphylum
ships.description: Navarch society's vision of luxury rarely matches up with that of humanity's; particularly in the way that a "lavish" lifestyle in Navarch society is often described as serving aboard a large, powerful vessel, rather than spending most of their golden years on a rich planet surrounded by other rich folks. However, there is a subset of Navarch culture that doesn't mind a bit of extra comfort, and many of them end up travelling aboard ships like the Microphylum. 	While the conditions aboard the ship aren't "luxurious" by most species' standards, the beds are at least big enough for any Navarch of reasonable size to comfortably sleep in, and there's more interesting food aboard than the taffylike rations Navarch crew often subsist off of.

ships.name: Imperium
ships.description: The Imperium-class Auxiliary makes the Republic Navy's own auxiliary look pitiful in comparison; carrying a formidable main battery in its own right with nearly triple the capacity of its smaller sibling on all fronts, the Imperium is a staple of large Navarch fleets.

ships.name: Dominium
ships.description: The Dominium is a large-scale freighter that entered Navarch space quite recently, dating back about half a millenium. Over the course of its short life, it has seen massive popularity in the Navarchs' shipping sectors, able to carry an enormous amount of cargo wherever its needed. It is quite the sluggish ship, but Navarch captains are no stranger to bulky, slow ships.

ships.name: Quarg Battleproteus
ships.description: These are light, blindingly fast automatons used by the Quarg. On death, they overload their antimatter core, causing an uncharacteristically massive explosion.

variants.name: Quarg Wardragon (Automaton)
variants.description: The Wardragon is used by the Quarg as a light warship. It is an older design within the Quarg's fleets, supposedly less intimidating compared to their larger warships and thus more suitable for dealings with particularly nascent species.

variants.name: Quarg Wardragon (Automaton, Missile)
variants.description: The Wardragon is used by the Quarg as a light warship. It is an older design within the Quarg's fleets, supposedly less intimidating compared to their larger warships and thus more suitable for dealings with particularly nascent species.

variants.name: Quarg Wardragon (Automaton, Offense)
variants.description: The Wardragon is used by the Quarg as a light warship. It is an older design within the Quarg's fleets, supposedly less intimidating compared to their larger warships and thus more suitable for dealings with particularly nascent species.

variants.name: Quarg Battleproteus (Missile)
variants.description: These are light, blindingly fast automatons used by the Quarg. On death, they overload their antimatter core, causing an uncharacteristically massive explosion.

outfits.name: Half-Notch Fusion Cell
outfits.description: A Navarch reactor squeezed into as small of a space as possible, with a capacitor integrated directly into the energy loop. This serves as the power source for the Navarchs' drones, but would be able to supply energy for the fighters or interceptors of a lesser faction.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Thruster (Tiny)
outfits.description: Despite their usage of large, heavy ships, Navarch engines are rather refined. Instead of providing as much thrust as possible, these engines are only about as powerful as plasma engines, but sharply reduce the effectiveness of enemy displacing attacks.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Thruster (Small)
outfits.description: This small nanoplasma thruster is the standard for Navarch fighters, and serves a secondary role on many of their larger ships. In addition to a moderate amount of kick, these engines include billions of nanothrusters that counteract the displacing effects of incoming attacks.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Thruster (Medium)
outfits.description: This nanoplasma thruster is in an odd spot, size-wise; too big for fighters, too small for ships. However, it serves a critical role as a benchmark for performance tests.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Thruster (Large)
outfits.description: These large nanoplasma thrusters are capable of pushing some of the Navarchs' lighter warships at significant speeds, but lack the grunt needed to move their largest ships.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Thruster (Huge)
outfits.description: As large as some of the largest engines humans have ever built, these nanoplasma thrusters are capable of significantly offsetting an opponent's attempts to push a ship away.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Thruster (Giant)
outfits.description: These enormous thrusters are the primary propulsion method for most Navarch warships; larger than the interceptors of some species, this set of thrusters will get any ship where it needs to go.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Steering (Tiny)
outfits.description: Sometimes even the Navarchs just have a little space left over to adjust their ships' agility; these tiny engines are inadequate even for their fighters, but serve moderately well as tweaks to a larger engine set.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Steering (Small)
outfits.description: This is the standard steering system for Navarch fighters, and for good reason; it provides decent thrust for its size, while being compact and providing resistance against enemy displacement attacks.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Steering (Medium)
outfits.description: Commonly used as a secondary steering system, this medium-sized nanoplasma thruster offers good all-around performance. Like its sister thruster, it is often used as a benchmarking device.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Steering (Large)
outfits.description: A nanoplasma engine of this size is said to contain more micro-propulsion blocks than a standard human body has cells. As such, it's no surprise that it's powerful while providing utility in the form of protecting from unexpected jerks in spaceflight as well as engine interference.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Steering (Huge)
outfits.description: This steering system is generally either adequate or too large for most ships produced by the Navarchs, providing any ship a noticeable increase in agility while reducing the likelihood that an enemy attack leaves a ship still in the sky.

outfits.name: Nanoplasma Steering (Giant)
outfits.description: The largest nanoplasma steering set is reserved only for the largest of ships assembled by the Navarchs. Navarchs commonly joke that engines like these would be terrifying weapons, if only they had a practical amount of range.

outfits.name: Pantheon-Class Breach Sealant
outfits.description: When the Navarchs needed a shield generator for their largest ships, they sought to make a shield generator that would be able to level the playing field with any alien armada. This shield generator is so powerful that the shield often leaks into the hull, effectively replacing lost surface hull until a more permanent fix can be implemented.

outfits.name: Temple-Class Breach Sealant
outfits.description: The Temple-Class Breach Sealant is a mid-sized breach sealing system, intended either for middleweight warships or as a support to a larger Pantheon-class on a larger ship.

outfits.name: Throne-Class Breach Sealant
outfits.description: Utilizing techniques discovered during the creation of the larger Pantheon-Class Breach Sealant, the Throne-Class is a far smaller rig designed for small torpedo boats or fighters. A little over one-tenth the size of the Pantheon-Class, the Throne-Class serves its role well.

outfits.name: "Kecid" Rearmorer
outfits.description: This larger rearmorer is capable of repairing even the largest Navarch ships in a fraction of the time that a breach sealant unit of comparable size would, but requires an enormous amount of energy to keep running and has no ability to recover a ship's shields.

outfits.name: "Lythang" Rearmorer
outfits.description: Experimental Navarch vessels rely primarily on their cutting-edge armor rather than shield matricies. These odd "hull reactors" contain loops that allow them to circulate a gel that solidifies and crystallizes into this new armor when exposed to open space, allowing a ship to repair itself at great speed. The system takes a constant supply of energy to fabricate and circulate replacement fluid, but as a consequence, requires very little active energy when the hull is damaged.

outfits.name: "Prathon" Rearmorer
outfits.description: Experimental Navarch vessels rely primarily on their cutting-edge armor rather than shield matricies. These odd "hull reactors" contain loops that allow them to circulate a gel that solidifies and crystallizes into this new armor when exposed to open space, allowing a ship to repair itself at great speed. The system takes a constant supply of energy to fabricate and circulate replacement fluid, but as a consequence, requires very little active energy when the hull is damaged.

outfits.name: 20x Fusion Reactor
outfits.description: Though the design was not ever intended for reactors larger than the 10x, the Navarchs' super battleship design required energy beyond the realm of the 10x. This colossal rig's power output is enough to run a moderately sized spaceport.

outfits.name: 14x Fusion Reactor
outfits.description: Though the design was not ever intended for reactors larger than the 10x, the Navarchs' super battleship design required energy beyond the realm of the 10x. This colossal rig's power output is enough to run a moderately sized spaceport.

outfits.name: 10x Fusion Reactor
outfits.description: Once the largest reactor the Navarchs produced, the shift to overall larger vessels (over the mid-sized vessels once favoured by Navarch doctrine) has resulted in this reactor being just a medium-sized permutation of the typical Navarch fusion technology.

outfits.name: 6x Fusion Reactor
outfits.description: This smaller reactor serves as a secondary power source for the Navarchs' larger vessels.

outfits.name: 4x Fusion Reactor
outfits.description: This small fusion reactor serves as a midstep between the Navarchs' fighter-scale reactors and their much larger capital ship reactors, often not large enough to power a ship by itself, but small enough it can serve as a secondary reactor.

outfits.name: 2x Fusion Reactor
outfits.description: For their fighters, the Navarchs simply scaled down their pre-existing reactor design. This isn't a particularly elegant solution, but provides the necessary energy to run all of a Subvarietas' systems and weapons.

outfits.name: 1x Fusion Reactor
outfits.description: This is a miniscule generator by Navarch standards, allowing their smallest ships to boast significant electrical output while remaining compact.

outfits.name: 1/2x Reactor Cell
outfits.description: A Navarch Fusion reactor crammed into as small of a package as possible. The resultant system runs fairly warm, even for its size, but produces all the energy needed to run a Subforma drone and all of its faculties.

outfits.name: Cluster Battery
outfits.description: Named after collections of galaxies in space, this huge battery is capable of storing an alarming amount of energy.

outfits.name: Galaxy Battery
outfits.description: Whether used as a support to a larger battery pack or on its own, this battery grants its host ship a significant boost to energy capacity.

outfits.name: Planet Battery
outfits.description: This battery is only suitable for medium or light warships employed by the Navarchs, but for most other species, its size and capacity would better fit large capital warships.

outfits.name: Moon Battery
outfits.description: This relatively compact battery is used by small Navarch ships with low energy needs, such as their light carriers.

outfits.name: Accretion Capacitor
outfits.description: This larger capacitor was designed by the Navarchs for small ships with inconsistent energy needs, such as those fielding lots of anti-missile.

outfits.name: Comet Capacitor
outfits.description: This is a moderately sized capacitor, designed by the Navarchs for their fighters.

outfits.name: "Kepilora" Nominal Storage
outfits.description: Reserved for particularly large experimental vessels, this Nominal Storage system is capable of providing a good source of shields to any ship it's installed on; it does, however, run quite hot.

outfits.name: "Lycir" Nominal Storage
outfits.description: Though the Navarchs understand them well-enough to build them regularly, the exact workings of the Nominal Storage are a mystery to the human mind. The best explanation you've gotten is that the devices use a yottrite filament to trigger assorted actions in the battery during charging and discharging that produces shields and heat as a byproduct.

outfits.name: "Igirid" Nominal Storage
outfits.description: Nominal Storages are a curious set of devices cooked up by the Navarchs' experimental department; like normal batteries, they store energy, but the storage device itself produces a field as it charges and discharges, allow a ship to recover its shields passively without consuming any extra energy. 	Compared to typical Navarch batteries, Nominal Storages do not store quite as much energy per space, and generate some heat.

outfits.name: AHDU (Huge)
outfits.description: Particularly large Navarch battleships often find themselves installing many heat dissipation units. To attempt to simplify ship blueprints, the Navarchs designed this most impressive cooling system.

outfits.name: AHDU (Large)
outfits.description: This large implementation of the Advanced Heat Dissipation Unit is a powerful cooling system designed to offset the significant heat produced by their battleships.

outfits.name: AHDU (Medium)
outfits.description: This large implementation of the Advanced Heat Dissipation Unit is a powerful cooling system designed to offset the significant heat produced by their battleships.

outfits.name: AHDU (Small)
outfits.description: This small Heat Dissipation Unit is designed as a small add-on for most Navarch Vessels, but has use as primary cooling on some of their smallest ships.

outfits.name: Fuel Distillery
outfits.description: Because their ships are designed to operate both in- and out-of-atmosphere, the Navarchs have a particular distaste towards solar-reliant systems, and ramscoops are no exception. This large device distills fuel over time, allowing a ship to refuel even when solar energy is nonpresent. 	Due to the fact that its size and cooling requirements are on par with a midsized nuclear reactor, it is found only on support ships.

outfits.name: Spectral Jammer
outfits.description: This jammer broadcasts broad-wave light across radar and visible wavelengths, making it far more difficult for missiles to maintain a lock.

outfits.name: Analysis Scope
outfits.description: The Navarchs engage in combat at distances far greater than most species, so their scanners are tuned to work at extreme ranges. Despite only being twice the size of a human tactical scanner, this advanced scope is nearly 8 times as powerful.

outfits.name: Mass Mineral Proc Array
outfits.description: A typical Navarch mining fleet includes one central carrier responsible co-ordinating the entire fleet, and part of those duties include procing all asteroids in the vacinity for valuable minerals. This powerful scanner consumes some energy, but provides an unreal level of asteroid scanning.

outfits.name: Navarch Boarding Supremacy
outfits.description: With the claws in their arms acting as electrified harpoons, the Navarchs rarely have a need for artificial weapons; not to mention, they are unlikely to refuse to sell their technology to others, for the right price. However, should someone attempt to capture a Navarch ship by force, this labyrinthine network of choke-points, hidden flanks, automated defenses, and heavy gear for on-board personnel awaits them.

outfits.name: Quarg Loatherift
outfits.description: This unassuming outfit acts as a locus for powerful teleporters aboard Quarg ringworlds, allowing Quarg ships to warp in massive amounts of ultra-powerful missiles without worrying about running out of ammunition. The teleporter, however, does require significant energy and cooling to operate safely.

outfits.name: 14-103 Twin Battery
outfits.description: For their super battleships, the Navarchs designed this huge-bore turret. Though the reload time leaves much to be desired, the huge shots deliver crushing damage over a broad area; each shell could level a medium-sized human warship.

outfits.name: 10-77 Twin Battery
outfits.description: This is the primary weapon for the Navarchs' large battleships: a twin-barreled, wide-bore cannon that's slow to aim and fire but deals impeccable damage once it connects. The significant firing forces produced by the weapon require a special armored hardpoint (a barbette) to be installed.

outfits.name: 7-62 Twin Battery
outfits.description: This weapon is a far smaller caliber than its bigger brother, but has a longer relative barrel length to compensate, allowing its projectiles to fly similar distances despite their lighter payload. Despite the major downsizing, this turret still produces enough force when firing to require a barbette.

outfits.name: 4-26 Dual Turret
outfits.description: The 4-26 is designed as a secondary turret for the Navarchs' large battleships, or a more primary role for their smaller ships. One turret is not particularly impressive by itself, but when equipped en masse, they can be effective at wearing down opponents at a fair distance.

outfits.name: 1-18 Anti-Fighter Rig
outfits.description: For anti-fighter roles, this tiny, snappy turret is the Navarchs' first choice. Small enough to be mounted on nearly anything and capable of a freakishly high rate of fire, this turret is designed for close-ranged anti-swarm combat, with a wild spray and considerable damage output.

outfits.name: 1-24 Anti-Fighter Array
outfits.description: Developed for the Regio-class carrier, this larger implementation of the 1-18 model autocannon is designed to saturate an area in anti-fighter fire. Improvements to the design also include greatly improved velocity, and subsequently, increased range.

outfits.name: THEL Node
outfits.description: The Navarchs have relatively little experience with beam technology compared to their tried and true "energy shell" designs. This prototypical weapon (dubbed the Tactical High Energy Laser) is their first such combat-practical design; a huge beam that carves through all but the thickest armor in its path, though compared to its projectile-based bretheren it suffers in the shield damage department. 	While the weapon doesn't produce nearly as much firing force as its projectile-based counterparts, the energy and cooling requirements means it still needs a barbette to be handled properly.

outfits.name: Shock Blaster Delta
outfits.description: Shock Blasters were designed as a method of building turrets that could provide effective damage at range without needing a barbette. The Shock Blaster Delta is the largest design that was successful in its goal: A rapid-fire, anti-area blaster that drains the electrical energy of struck ships, able to be mounted on any ship with the capacities to support it and capable of long-distance operations.

outfits.name: 5-36 Bombardier
outfits.description: Found aboard the newly developed Subformae, these modest cannons are capable of delivering significant anti-capital damage, with the sophisticated projectile shapes causing a small amount of damage to hull regardless of the target's shield state.

outfits.name: 3-22 Bombardier
outfits.description: A highly specialized cannon designed for fighter-to-capital warfare. Though slightly smaller caliber than its battleship-mounted cousins, the 3-22 Bombardier is outfitted with armor-piercing projectile forms that cause immense damage on impact at the cost of poor performance against crowds. 	To counteract the considerable hit force buildup that can accrue on a target under fire from a large swarm of Subvarietas, the Navarchs have designed this weapon to pull a target slightly closer to the ship, significantly reducing the likelihood a sortie of Subvarietas will be kited away from their support fleet.

outfits.name: 0.6-16 Autocannon
outfits.description: An autocannon designed for use aboard the Subvarietas fighter. Though its per-shot damage is notably unimpressive, it is capable of a blistering rate of fire with shells that have a deceptively wide danger area, making it excellent for interfighter combat.

outfits.name: "Povenant" Anti-Scuttle
outfits.description: Anti-Scuttles are area-of-effect devices that produce a powerful shield recovery effect during combat. Though even this small model of Anti-Scuttle requires a substantial amount of space and energy generation to operate, it is capable of recovering the shields of surrounding ships rather readily. Though the physical "ring" of influence highlights where the Anti-Scuttle is most effective, the rig's radius of effect caps out at about double what is observable to the naked eye. Because they operate on similar principles to Breach Sealant, Anti-Scuttles are also capable of repairing some of a ship's hull (though at a greatly diminished rate, and only within the visible ring).

outfits.name: Monolithic Anti-Missile
outfits.description: This Anti-Missile system is specially designed for carriers or other ships with few hardpoints, but otherwise large capacity for weapons. Though the Formidable Anti-Missile offers more balanced performance, the Monolithic model has supreme range, allowing it to cast a wide net of defense over an allied fleet.

outfits.name: Formidable Anti-Missile
outfits.description: The Formidable Anti-Missile is the standard-issue missile defense system for Navarch ships. Though it doesn't quite pack as much punch-per-ton as its smaller brother, it has greater range and higher per-shot power, massively increasing the likelihood a single shot will be needed to thwart a missile.

outfits.name: Intimidating Anti-Missile
outfits.description: Designed for light ships with a large amount of hardpoints, the Intimidating Anti-Missile is the smallest anti-missile system offered by the Navarchs. Its range is quite unimpressive compared to their larger anti-missile systems, but allows a ship to keep itself clear of enemy missile barrages.

outfits.name: Phase Torpedo
outfits.description: Named for their ability to move through space, air, or water, these heavy torpedoes consume massive amounts of energy and move slowly, but inflict devastating damage on hit, to the point where no shield can prevent at least some hull damage from leaking through.

outfits.name: Lathe Mine Bay
outfits.description: Lathe Mines are a particularly brutal type of obstacle that the Navarchs designed to be laid out in great numbers, dealing crushing damage to any ship who dares to stumble into them. Using similar technology to the phase torpedo, Lathe Mines cause heavy damage even through shields. The unique design of the Lathe mines means that, though they're intended as a trap, they are capable of serving as a form of anti-area projectile in the right conditions.

outfits.name: Ransacker ALS
outfits.description: Ransacker Missiles are a surprisingly unrefined weapon; easily replaceable missiles that split into a wide barrage of smaller explosives, pelting enemy fleets with an enormous amount of cluster munitions. 	Ransackers are launched at a reduced launch pressure, reducing load on the ship and allowing 9 to be launched from a relatively compact platform. However, the fact that the projectiles are assembled on the spot means reload time leaves something to be desired.

outfits.name: Hyperdrive Malformer
outfits.description: True to its name, this weapon works in a similar method to a commonplace hyperdrive; it uses a large quantity of deuterium to produce a large explosion. However, instead of tucking it into a safe region of spacetime to accelerate the ship, the device warps the explosion a good distance in front of the firing ship, causing a devastating explosion. According to Navarch legend, this was the weapon that caused the Drak and Quarg to seal the Navarchs away. 	Somehow, the Navarchs have found a way to program the explosion in a way that it doesn't harm allied ships, meaning that, for a weapon of mass destruction, it's surprisingly safe to use.

outfits.name: Unbound Gauss Slug
outfits.description: This three-ton hunk of yottrite alloy is ammunition for the Unbound Gauss Drive. The acceleration the slugs experience is intense enough to distend the slug over the course of firing, but the result is an unstoppable column of destruction that cuts through all in its path.

outfits.name: Unbound Gauss Drive
outfits.description: The earliest phases of this weapon's development harken back to before the Navarchs even first came into contact with the Quarg; an early attempt at using energy to replace the fuel in a Hyperdrive's operation, allowing a planet to theoretically launch fighters without any need for deuterium or worry of fallout from the fusion explosion that powers a Hyperdrive. The device failed, and was shelved for millenia. 	Relatively recently, however, some attention was brought back to the device, with the hopes that it could be turned into an effective weapon against swarms of Quarg Automata. The resultant weapon fires enormous yottrite-alloy slugs at near-light speed, causing an explosive effect on target and effortlessly cutting through all in its way. 	(Note: The amount of contact per shot can vary with enemy size, so damage per second is approximate.)

description.text: Arragat Harbor acts largely as a reserve shipyard for its host planet, but also serves as the single largest outrigger interchange point for Navarch captains looking to adjust their fleets' capabilities before heading out on more missions. As such, it is quite busy here, despite the relative inelegance of Navarch stations compared to their terrestrial worlds.

spaceport.text: The station is almost entirely spaceport, with artificial gravity being the only thing from keeping cargo and personnel from tumbling off the platforms. Numerous small tug drones work to expediently guide interchanging outriggers between ships, and a few Navarchs can be seen taking pictures of the bright trails left behind by the small nanoplasma thrusters the tugs use.

description.text: This is one of the few worlds with enough notable landmass for the Navarchs to have built landbound ship facilities. Besides that, it is also a super-ocean world, with a surface area nearly 6 times larger than Earth, nearly 98% of which is water. As such, it serves as the perfect staging ground for the Navarchs' massive warfleets.

spaceport.text: The spaceport sprawls all over and around a lone continent around the size of south america; large ships wait at port around the coast, with several channels reserved for ships coming in for landing. Each dock here could hold 5-6 human ships of any size.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is entirely seabound, with large "runways" for ships to land on the water. As expected, the scope is truly massive; each dock here is roughly six times the size of the largest human space docks.

spaceport.text: The spaceport on Pechora is highly organized and automated; even the Navarchs' largest cargo ships are very swiftly loaded with kilotons of refined metals for export.

description.text: Fochexa is a warm ocean world with high, sharp spires of rock that stretch from the ocean floor to the surface, forming small islands anywhere from a few feet to a mile across. These landmasses aren't large enough to establish any sort of presence on, but they do lend the Navarchs a helping hand when it comes to monitoring the drifting of the spaceport.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is a sprawling complex of docks and channels, serving many military fleets as they pass through here. This planet serves as a critical chokepoint, and as such, is heavily guarded.

Beaufort's value comes from the presence of yottrite in its home system, which the Navarchs use in their ships and weapons.

spaceport.text: Beaufort's spaceport seems to have been formed of molten metal slag like much of the rest of its surface, with natural outcrops serving as docking bays. Though the planet's surface is surprisingly temperate and has enough gravity to hold the water channels in place, it has no noticeable atmosphere.

description.text: Norvik is a large ocean world ripe with many rare and exotic metals, and is a critical mining planet for the Navarchs; however, twice an orbit, the moon "dips" in the rings of its parent planet, causing horrific meteor showers. As such, all ships staioned here are above a certain size, to avoid damage incurred by the showers.

spaceport.text: The spacport here consists only of large docks, and are heavily reinforced; in fact, you aren't walking along the metal structure at all, but instead shields over 2 feet thick. Meteoroids of various sizes are littered throughout the spaceport's scaffoldlike walkways, and there always seems to be some part under repair.

description.text: Beneath a thick layer of fog lies a planet with a vibrant rest-hued ocean, coloured so because of the absurdly high iron content of the water. Navarch ships here have to land with shields fully enabled to avoid iron particulate clinging to the exterior of their hulls. The iron here is, in fact, so infused into the water, that occasionally large enough storm clouds will have the mineral content necessary to rain iron as if it were clean water, requiring all of the ships and buildings here to run their shields all the time to avoid being petrified like the few small species of tree native to the islands.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is encased in a large, domular shield that protects it from the "rust rain". Despite this, there is a rather robust shipyard located here, taking advantage of the practically limitless sources of raw materials in the waters and small islands around the spaceport.

spaceport.text: Unlike other Navarch Stations, there is a suprising amount of non-dock station here, with vast interior spaces used for mineral processing and storage. The working population here exceeds some human planets, with a few pamphlets boasting a figure of "800,000 strong arms in the workplace family".

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is fairly small, hosted vertically along some large cliff faces, with docks that float somewhat freely on the water to avoid fighting the jostling tides. Fleet positions here are fairly uncommon, except for military contractors testing prototype works.

description.text: The Navarchs aren't much for luxurious living, instead preferring to show off their status with impressive private militias. However, Cantabri is one of the few worlds reserved for the elite who doesn't want to spend their whole life aboard a cruising vessel. The planet's seas are a rich blue, and are calm enough that you can see your reflection in them. The Navarchs here are a slightly uppity sort compared to most you've met, but the mood here is overall pleasant and tranquil.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is built in a specifically reserved sect of ocean, leaving the rest of the waters placid for the locals to enjoy. The market here deals in lots of luxury goods, and most Navarchs here seem to be of a significantly different caste than the hard-working naval crews or the diligent researchers, and most attempt to stop you to tell you stories of their "past lives" as one of such roles.

description.text: Byscay is an ocean world buried under thick fog. Apparently, it was one of the first worlds the Navarchs settled post-exile, contributing to why all Navarch ships have overly powerful two-way telemetry transmitters.

spaceport.text: Hidden in the fog is the spaceport, where conditions are nearly white-out. You can't comfortably see from one side of a dock to another, and it seems the locals don't fare much better, as powerful spotlights are a feature every few yards. The locals here all have loud conversations as they work, presumably to give eachother ample notice of their location.

description.text: A warm ocean planet tidally locked with its parent brown dwarf, Straido is home to a large maritime city that's responsible for exports of fish across a good swathe of Navarch space. The population here exceeds 100 billion individuals, and the planet is remarkably self-sufficient compared to similarly urban human worlds.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is designed mostly for cargo and logistical ships rather than warships, so capital warships are typically serviced by intraplanetary shuttlecraft that use the deck space on such warships as landing pads. Despite this, orders are conducted with surprising efficiency, with many ships hosting shuttles even before they've come to rest in the water.

description.text: A snow world, Blihano is valued for the pelts of its native creatures, which are used to make exotic textiles. Hunting here is carefully regulated to ensure the species here aren't overhunted. Despite this, it remains a popular sporting world, and a spaceport in a small, artificial ocean a few hundred miles in any direction serves most of the planet.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is confined to a small ocean kept artificially melted by ships with special heat rays. Small boats trawl the surface, blasting ice back into a liquid form. The residents here have many stories about ships being damaged by the ice refreezing.

description.text: Leload Station is a mining platform that was built by the Navarchs to take advantage of the colossal amount of raw resources available in the system; as a consequence, however, Leiload System is the subject of frequent asteroid impacts, and thus heavy defenses are necessary; some of the turrets here are sourced from the research centers nearby, using the station as a testbed for long-ranged cannons and other such things.

spaceport.text: Unlike other Navarch Stations, there is a suprising amount of non-dock station here, with vast interior spaces used for mineral processing and storage. The working population here exceeds some human planets, with a few pamphlets boasting a figure of "800,000 strong arms in the workplace family".

description.text: A warm ocean planet tidally locked with its parent brown dwarf, Straido is home to a large maritime city that's responsible for exports of fish across a good swathe of Navarch space. The population here exceeds 100 billion individuals, and the planet is remarkably self-sufficient compared to similarly urban human worlds.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is designed mostly for cargo and logistical ships rather than warships, so capital warships are typically serviced by intraplanetary shuttlecraft that use the deck space on such warships as landing pads. Despite this, orders are conducted with surprising efficiency, with many ships hosting shuttles even before they've come to rest in the water.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is fairly small, hosted vertically along some large cliff faces, with docks that float somewhat freely on the water to avoid fighting the jostling tides. Fleet positions here are fairly uncommon, except for military contractors testing prototype works.

description.text: A snow world, Blihano is valued for the pelts of its native creatures, which are used to make exotic textiles. Hunting here is carefully regulated to ensure the species here aren't overhunted. Despite this, it remains a popular sporting world, and a spaceport in a small, artificial ocean a few hundred miles in any direction serves most of the planet.

description.text: Byscay is an ocean world buried under thick fog. Apparently, it was one of the first worlds the Navarchs settled post-exile, contributing to why all Navarch ships have overly powerful two-way telemetry transmitters.

spaceport.text: Hidden in the fog is the spaceport, where conditions are nearly white-out. The locals here all have loud conversations as they work, presumably to give eachother ample notice of their location.

description.text: The Navarchs aren't much for luxurious living, instead preferring to show off their status with impressive private militias. However, Cantabri is one of the few worlds reserved for the elite who doesn't want to spend their whole life aboard a cruising vessel. The planet's seas are a rich blue, and are calm enough that you can see your reflection in them. The Navarchs here are a slightly uppity sort compared to most you've met, but the mood here is overall pleasant and tranquil.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is built in a specifically reserved sect of ocean, leaving the rest of the waters placid for the locals to enjoy. description.text: Bayja is an ocean moon that exhibits extremely strong tidal actions due to the gravity of its host planet; the tides here can exceed a grade of 5 degrees during the "close" part of the planet's rotation. As such, permanent settlements are a rarity here, with most livingspaces just being retired military ships (some of which are old enough that they are no longer sold in Navarch space).

spaceport.text: The "spaceport" is essentially just a Supravitae that has had most of its weapons stripped off in favour of marketplaces and communications equipment, co-ordinating the thousands of independent houseboats on-world. Some free-floating raftlike boats exist to serve trade between fleets, driven by smaller versions of the nanoplasma engines used on ships.

description.text: Cagliari is a mining outpost that forgot to stop growing about a millenium ago. It is now one of the largest, most populous worlds in Navarch space, owing its prosperity to an absurdly high mineral content in the system it inhabits. Additionally, Cagliari supplies some exotic materials to research systems nearby, earning it a fair pay in the open market. It is for this reason that the Navarchs widely refer to this planet as their "home away from home", despite the fact that the planet doesn't even have a proper shipyard; just a basic station for supplying and outfitting logistical vessels.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is constructed around long fjords, where logistical ships can come to a low cruising speed and still be serviced by the time they reach the opening at the other end of the fjords the supply depots are built around. In this way, it is very rare that cargo jams happen, as ships are constantly on the move through well-organized supply lines.

children.key: You're caught off guard by the size of the spaceport as you come in for landing, having to land on what appears to be a few fighter pads instead of a true ship dock. As you step out, a few of the locals approach you; they're large, eel-like folks, with dark black skin with lighter, pale-green fronts, with long tails ending in large horns. Their clothing looks as though it's intricately woven from individual straps of cloth, formed somewhat tightly to the wearer's body. It accentuates the fact that even the smallest of the locals among you stand a good 2 or 3 feet taller than you, with large builds to match.
After a few moments of quiet pondering from both you and the alien, it speaks in slightly warbly, but otherwise coherent english. "Well now, you aren't a Quarg, are ya?" They ask.
"I am, I just got the small genes in the family."
"I'm a human, why would I be a Quarg?"
"Would me being a Quarg be a problem?"
The eel alien (and a few of their nearby compatriots) laughs. "No way you're a Quarg; they're too high and mighty to joke about that," They remark, "So, what exactly are ya?"
"I'm not one for giving out personal details to aliens; what are you?"
The eel alien nods. "Well, put simply, the only visitors we get are Quarg coming to make sure we aren't plotting anything 'dangerous', and they only come around so often," They explain.
"Why do the Quarg come and visit you?"

"Problem's a strong word for it," The eel states, "But the Quarg exiled us a long time ago, and now the only time we get visitors is when they come to make sure we're not doing anything 'in violation of better judgement'."
A few of the other eels snort and snarl in response to the latter part of the sentence; it seems the Quarg aren't popular around here.

"A human, eh?" The eel leans down a bit to examine you, "Yeah, you fit the bill. The Quarg send snippets through their automata; to try and 'entice us to give up our weapons of mass destruction'," The alien says.

"The Quarg and the Drak they serve don't exactly like our big, fancy explosive teleporters; they say it's 'a danger on a stellar scale', and that 'for peace to reign, they must be destroyed'. So, when we refused to give up our plans, they and the Archons rallied up and forced us to the far reaches of the galaxy," The alien explains.
"Well, that's why you're here, but what are you?"
"Yeah, the Quarg can be a bit of a buzzkill like that."
"You'd rather be exiled rather than giving up one weapon?"

"Our greatest weapon: The ability to take the explosion that powers a hyper- or scram-drive, and force it back into the physical world, causing an explosion capable of destabilizing a star with enough fuel. The shipboard versions of the weapon don't have nearly enough energy to do that kind of damage, but the Quarg and Drak saw the first prototypes and demanded that we either give them up or get out," The alien says.
"Well, that's why you're here, but what are you?"
"Yeah, the Quarg can be a bit of a buzzkill like that."
"You'd rather be exiled rather than giving up one weapon?"

"Well, we formally declared war on the Quarg," The eel explains, "A war that we never agreed to end. So, we began researching jump drives to return to the Quarg and once again engage them in battle; when they found out, they agreed to give us an adversary to entertain our ideals with."
"What kind of ideals require you to go to war?"
"Yeah, the Quarg can be a bit of a buzzkill like that."
"Well, that's what you believe in, but what are you?"

"In our culture, there is no higher honor than being formally engaged in war, and one tenet of that is that surrender must be mutual in a way that both parties see benefit from," The eel explains, "When the Quarg demanded we either give up our weaponry or leave our home turf, we had an ideological obligation to not surrender our plans, at least without a fair trade; a trade they refused to entertain."
A few of the other eels contribute stories of how the Quarg demanded all sacrifice and no compensation.
"Yeah, the Quarg can be a bit of a buzzkill like that."
"Well, that's what you believe in, but what are you?"

The eel snorts and laughs in response, "Aye, isn't that the truth?" They suppose, chuckling, a few of their compatriots contributing some sort of chant, "You're quite the sight for sore eyes with that sort of outlook."
"So who are you, exactly?" You ask.

The eel smiles, "Ah, we are the Navarchs; masters of the seas and indomitable of spirit," They introduce. "You're welcome to visit our space and purchase our technology, traveller; our time in exile has yielded a vast bounty; one we're willing to share with those of open mind and intentions."
"You just... Let strangers buy your technology?"
"Is there anything I should know about your space?"
"I hope to be able to see all you have to offer; I think I'll go now."

"Well, of course. Cultures were not made to exist in solitude and silence; buy our technology, and show it to all; when the time comes for the war of legends, we wish to learn from both our allies and our enemies," The Navarch says.
"Is there anything I should know about your space?"
"I hope to be able to see all you have to offer; I think I'll go now."

The Navarch looks on wistfully, "There will come a time when our galaxy will meet a threat beyond any one faction or species; a war where two galaxies' worth of life goes in, and only one galaxy's life survives. When that happens, we want all factions in our galaxy to be ready, not just us."
"What a terrifying prophecy. I hope that never comes to pass."
"Should I know anything else before I explore your territory?"
"We can only hope, human. Did you have any other questions for us?" The Navarch asks.
"Should I know anything else before I explore your territory?"
"I don't have anymore questions; I think I'll go now."

The Navarch thinks for a long moment. "Hmm... Well, you should probably know that our space has occasional pockets of systems that only have one entrance or exit; it can be a problem if you want to get somewhere quickly," The Navarch says.

The Navarch then perks up, "Ah, you should take some time to map out the wormholes in our space; most of 'em are tucked in dead ends, but they can be mighty handy if you need to slip somewhere quickly; not to mention it saves on fuel," He adds.
"Thank you for your advice; I think I'll go now."
As you land on <planet>, you notice a Quarg ship closely following behind you. As you dock, several Quarg exit the ship, and walk towards yours. Nervously, you exit the hatch of your own ship.
One of the Quarg speaks up, "We understand that you have, as of recent, unlocked the wormhole gating the Navarchs from the rest of the galaxy," The Quarg says.
"I did? Ma just raised me to push buttons when I see them."
"As a matter of fact, you can," The Quarg states, "Recently, you've been recorded unlocking the wormhole to the Navarchs and contacting them; is this true?" They ask.
"Oh, so that's what the buttons did."

The Quarg stare at you for a long moment, clearly not buying that you did all of this "coincidentally". The Quarg in front sighs, "Well, regardless of your intent, please observe their culture with caution, rather than a desire to replicate it."
"They seemed fairly relaxed, to me. They just like big guns."
"They said you exiled them to the fringes."

The Quarg all stare at you for a long moment, as if deciding questioning you further is worth their time. Eventually, one of the Quarg sighs, "To put it simply, please do not seek to replicate their warlike, militarized ways. They are exiled for a reason," The Quarg insists.
"They seemed fairly relaxed, to me. They just like big guns."
"They said you exiled them to the fringes."

The Quarg share a brief glance among one another. "Well, you returned in one piece without a full Navarch invasion fleet, so it's hard to say so. Please, however, observe their warlike tendencies as a cautionary interest, rather than a lifestyle to be emulated," The Quarg requests.
"They seemed fairly chill, to me. They just like big guns."
"They said you exiled them to the fringes."

The Quarg gives you a curious glance. "Hm. Perhaps the eyes of a young race see it differently than we do after thousands of years of war across the galaxy," They suppose, chattering among themselves for a moment, before abruptly beginning to leave, one saying "Thank you for your time," As they all plod off.

The Quarg sighs, "It was a necessary evil. A faction as large and powerful as the Navarchs are a danger to the galaxy; they were headed toward a future similar to many species who seek only to improve their war technology," The Quarg states.

Another Quarg chimes in, "The weapons they developed were not simple nuclear weapons or large-scale lasers. The ability to project an explosion anywhere in relatively near space is the sort of technology that can end entire stars," They detail.
"To me, it sounds like you exiled them out of fear of their strength."
"You've never considered just asking them to not scale it past a certain size?"
"I'll be sure not to provoke any more military development. I'll be going now."
The Quarg's skin visibly lights up for a moment with vibrant red and blue hues, before one eventually says, "Perhaps, in some small way, you are right," They admit, "But our decision is final."
The Quarg rather quickly leave after this, leaving you to contemplate their warnings.

The Quarg share a curious glance, before turning back to you. "Our policy against their weapons has been very 'ground-zero', as a human might say it. Diplomacy has never been an option with such powerful weapons in play," They admit.
"The Navarchs told me their belief is that surrender is only acceptable with compromise from both sides."
"It sounds to me like you took the nuclear option too soon."
"I suppose that's understandable. I'll stop wasting your time now."

The Quarg think for a moment, but quickly shake their heads, "Negotiation with our technology is not an option; our technology is too powerful, even for a faction that rivals our own strength," The Quarg says, "Now, that's enough. You may go now, human," They state. Their tone is suddenly a bit hurried, as if they're considering what you said more than they let on, but they hustle away too quickly to follow up on the matter.

The Quarg share a short glance, then turn back to you. "An interesting opinion, but one we nor the Drak agree with," The Quarg says, "You may be on your way, now. Thank you for your time," They say, beginning to hustle back to their ship.
As you walk into the spaceport, there seems to be a significant amount of Navarchs here; given their general demeanor, they likely wouldn't take issue with you striking up some conversation.
A pair of Navarch dockworkers perk up as you approach. One of them speaks up, "Do you need something, human?" He asks.
"What's it like to work on such massive ships?"

The dockworks take a moment to ponder your question. "Well, it certainly keeps things busy," The first one remarks with a chuckle, "There's plenty of us to go around, though; work's easy when there's a few thousand of us handling any given task."
The other dockwork nods. "Usually, it's the small ships that give us trouble; when a Regio or an Epiregalimen land to get all their fighters fixed? THAT'S a handful," He laughs.
You nod a bit and take in the information, bantering with the dockworkers a bit more before preparing to leave.
One of the dockworks chuckles. "It's not often two days are exactly alike; each ship is big enough that we can go years without doing the exact same job," He replies.
His compatriot briefly turns to him. "Well, unless we're on fighter duty. That'd drive anybody insane," The second Navarch snorts.
"What's so bad about fighter duty?" You ask.

The second Navarch laughs. "Individually, not much, but I'm sure you've seen our carriers. When we've got some hundred fighters scheduled for full-maint, it's a scramble to get any and all deck space cleared out for all the incoming ships. Plus, we usually work in units on fighters, so it's not uncommon we're doing the same job several times in a row," He explains.

You nod a bit, unable to suppress a smile at the mental image of a human shipyard panicking to open up repair bays for the fighter payload of one of the big Navarch carriers. After a bit more less-interesting banter, you walk back to your ship.
You approach a Navarch in a particularly detailed uniform. He smiles at you, bearing many long, pointy teeth. "Ah, the visitor among us! How can I help you?" He asks.
"Did your kind always have those claws?"
"I'm curious as to your favorite ship, actually."

The Navarch's face turns into an earnest smile. "Well, 'hate' isn't the right word; we're warriors, and the Quarg are among the few races in the galaxy that we can comfortably call our equals," He explains, "We respect them as equals, and strive to engage them in combat. Quite frankly, I believe they wish the same, given that they've employed the automata to test our mettle."
You nod and ponder this for a moment; the Quarg despise war from what you've seen, yet the Navarch makes an interesting point.

The Navarch captain continues. "We've been told many times our warlike ways are unusual among the galaxy, so I can't blame your misunderstanding. I hope I've eased some of your concerns," He concludes, beginning to walk off.
You thank him for his time and head back to your ship.

The captain laughs. "Our bodies nowadays are more our own than nature's," The Navarch explains, "Our ancient ancestors were much more eel-like than we are now; much of our early history mentions a lack of legs, lackluster claws, and feeble, soft skin. However, that all changed during the Recreation: Our forefathers instituted a massive genetic engineering campaign. We evolved ourselves where nature refused to, into the much more land-friendly forms you see now."
You nod, unable to help but compare this to stories of the creation of the Alphas. You keep that comparison to yourself.
"Of course, we hold a great respect for those forebearers; even if their bodies were inferior, their minds were just as sharp as ours today; if not even moreso," He adds.
You thank the Navarch for his time and walk off.

Landing on this inconspicuous planet, you see a lone tower with a large terminal, featuring a large red button. Push it?

The button is heavy to the touch, and takes some heft to press it down. As you press it down, however... Nothing seems to happen, save for a few small chirps from the terminal. None of the symbols on the screen are intelligible to you.
Landing on this quiet planet, you see a lone tower with a large terminal, featuring a large green button. Push it?

The button feels cold to the touch, and you are labored with a great feeling of sorrow as you press it into the socket. The terminal chirps a bit as the button is pushed, but the lines pushed to the screen are unintelligible.
Landing on this lonely planet, you see a lone tower with a large terminal, featuring a large blue button. Push it?
The button has an unpleasant, damp texture, but practically falls into the socket as you press it. The terminal spits some garbled noises and prints some unreadable text.

children.key: While waiting for your ships to be refueled and restocked, you catch an advertisement for what seems to be a grand archive of Navarch ship designs. Care to have a peek?

After some asking around, you manage to find the archives. The building is massive; bigger than most industrial human buildings. Inside is a massive library, out of some sort of fantasy movie; the records here seem remarkably detailed. You could spend months reading and not even make a dent in the available material.

What strikes you is how calm and quiet it is inside, with any and all Navarch occupants being respectfully quiet. It seems some places are sacred ground, no matter how racketous a species' general temperament is.

You manage to squeeze your way between a few Navarch pedestrians who are also here to read and start walking down the aisles for something interesting. The archives are extensive; there's a whole aisle dedicated just to light warships with twenty to twenty five fighter bays, and another dedicated to warship-freighter hybrids in the four- to ten-thousand ton range.
Eventually, a Navarch wearing a sort of loose-fitted dress and an archive nametag smiles at you. "Are you looking for something in particular, human? You've been meandering for some time," She asks.

"Ah, you're just like the young ones; so curious," She says, a small bit of wistfulness in her voice, "Come with me," She says gently. You nod and follow her down several rows of books, until you find a small, cordoned off exhibit, festooned with not just books, but models as well.

"Though much of the archive is based on ships that were once built, we reserve this portion of the building for surviving scale-replicas and the most in-depth operations manuals," She explains, gesturing to the vast array of well-stocked tables, "Many of these are so detailed that a modern shipyard could reconstruct the ships within, given time and a budget."

The archivist's smile widens. "Well, not much," She supposes, "We have plenty of resources and manpower to go around, what with the Quarg Automata being a self-containing threat due to their lack of drives. I'm sure if you showed a properly detailed collection to the right team, they'd love the opportunity to experiment."

You nod contemplatively and begin browsing the prototypes section, looking over the more in-depth pieces. You question the rationale of trying to inspire an alien space to re-create ships from their past, but the Navarchs seem particularly open to having new things to do.

You find a particularly interesting model called the "Klados", which appears to be a modular warship of some sort. The scale model even reflects this, with "stackable" sections that allow you to make the ship either shorter and lighter, or longer and more well-armed.

The archivist, having followed you, smiles. "Ahh, the Klados... When our ancestors were at war with the Quarg, their researchers underwent a nearly explosive period of development; anything to act as a force multiplier. Electromagnetic hyperdrives, fuelless energy, and other such pursuits," She recalls, "I haven't read the journals in a long time, but if I recall correctly, the idea was to create a ship that could be built quickly in shipyards that expected Quarg attacks, but could be later expanded when time and supplies were more available."
You nod and take this all in. "Why didn't it ever get off the ground?" You ask.

"As I said, there was much innovation during that period. During that time, our shipbuilding doctrine shifted towards smaller, lighter vessels; many of the missile boats you see in space today can trace their ancestry to that time period," She elaborates, "When faced with ships that were effective against Quarg while requiring less materials, less workspace, and less training for captains to operate, the more complex design of the Klados was likely ruled out."
"That's a shame," You reply, "We have ships that use similar modularity to great effect."

"Perhaps you should show those old models and manuals to one of the industrial shipyards... Venif would be a good place. There are many shipyards with massive spare budgets waiting for interesting uses of their time," The archivist explains.
"You'd allow me to take them?" You ask.
"Of course. You don't think I'd suggest such a thing while prohibiting you from doing so, do you?" She asks, a sly smile on her face.
"I don't think I should be persuading you all to build more warships."

The archivist helps you gather the necessary models and journals in a padded bag for transport. "Keep them safe; they are not the originals, but we still value our history a great deal," She requests.
You thank her for her assistance and prepare to leave, winding through the numerous passages. Hopefully you remember where Venif is.

"I understand," The archivist replies with a disappointed nod, her smile fading, "As much as we would like to see you act more prominently in our space, the Quarg's judgment can be very harsh at times."
You nod a bit and thank her for her time regardless, preparing to wind your way through the archive's many halls.

You browse a bit longer, but don't find anything that particularly catches your eye. Eventually, you receive an alert that your ship is refueled, and you need to leave. You'll have to come dig again some other day.

As you touch down on Venif, you remember to take the Klados documentation with you, setting yourself on a mission to deliver them to one of the local shipyards. It takes some time for you to find a good directory, but you're soon on a shuttleboat to meet with with one of the smaller local shipyards, known as "Venalend Worksmiths".

Compared to more established Navarch shipyards, Venalend Worksmiths' yard is a relatively small afair, consisting of several floating docks and surrounding support structures. Despite this, it's still nearly twice the size of a typical human civilian shipyard, presumably for the sole purpose of sating the Navarchs' desire for particularly sizable ships.

You soon come face to face with a tall Navarch in what appears to be a work jumper. "Captain <last>! A pleasure to meet you in the flesh," She greets in a gruff, but jovial tone, firmly shaking your hand. You're not sure if it's a cultural thing, or if Navarchs are just that much stronger than humans, but the handshake leaves you trying to shake your fingers apart.

"I'm Staza; please, make yourself at home among my workspace," She introduces, still smiling. If there's one thing you appreciate about the Navarchs, it's that they rarely seem to be in a bad mood, "I heard you might have something for me and my crew here."
"I've got some plans from the archives for a ship called the Klados."

You offer Staza the bag of documentations and the model, and she takes it, settling it down on her desk with utmost care. A few other Navarchs crowd around, taking various journals and manuals. After what feels like a bit too long for what's presumably a cursory overlook, she turns to you and nods. "Yep, this is plenty to build from, alright," Staza eventually says.
Before you can answer, she gives a grin. "Now we just need some funding to start the project!"
"I seem to have forgotten my wallet."
"Would a hundred million credits get you started?"

Staza and some of her cohort laughs. "You don't need to worry about a thing, human," She says, still chuckling, "We aren't a greedy race; not in that manner, at least. Our space is bountiful, and our economy is mighty. Cultivating a prototype, or even a few, like this, is how we contribute to our culture, and the central markets pay good money for creativity and progress," Staza explains.

Staza laughs and shakes her head. "Relax, human, we don't expect to be bankrolled by one curious benefactor," She explains, "Our space is... Collaborative, one might say; everything feeds into everything else. For example, paying a foundry worker will make us alloy to build a ship that will transport a student to their new school so they can become a foundry worker," She explains, "So long as our ships can fly and our space can suit our needs for resources, curiosity and interest will be payment enough; at least for matters of speculation."
You nod a bit. "How soon can you have a prototype ready?" You ask.
Staza smiles. "Now that's a good question. We're not the largest team, but give us a month and change to secure resources and hammer something out. We'll give you a call when it's ready," She says.
You nod and thank her for her time, excitedly awaiting the new development. There's something about contributing to a species' development, even in a small way, that makes you giddy.

children.key: As you land on Venif, now landing at the coordinates given to you by Staza, you step out to greet her. She smiles a big, toothy grin and waves before looking out at the surprisingly moderately-sized vessel currently moored at one of the docks.
"Quite a looker for something so old, wouldn't you say?" She asks.
"Please never say 'looker' and 'old' in the same sentence again."

Staza laughs. "Well, if that's what you're worried about, there's two configurations larger than this one; modularity's a treat, let me tell you," She chuckles, "This configuration is just the smallest that'll let us test everything all at once."

Staza laughs hard enough that she's nearly doubled over, propping herself up on her desk. "And here I was told you had a sense of humour," She jokes, taking a deep breath and still snickering to herself as she resteadies herself, "Anyways, the design had to be modernized a bit to keep up with all our new technologies since the war; it's better than it's ever been."
"That's the spirit," Staza says, "Now all we have to do is test it out and make sure nothing's going to blow up except what it's shooting at."
You nod. "How do you plan to test it?" You ask.
Staza grins. "Well, I'm not the pilot between us," She says, "We're sending you into orbit with it and testing it against you!"
You gulp a bit, but nod. Hopefully you've the firepower to take it down.
"Just disable it, try not to blow it up. We've got soldiers on that ship," She remarks sternly. Again, you nod, and prepare to head back to your ship.

As you land, Staza and her crew are already looking over data being sent from the disabled testbed. "Excellent fighting, Captain; I see how you managed to get all the way out here," She compliments, grinning at you, "We've got everything we need, here. Not to mention, your fight with the ship has even drawn the eye of some curious admirals; we might have to upscale in the coming months!" She laughs.
You smile. "That's great news," You reply.
"Well, we're done with you for now; keep your eyes out. We might be ramping up production in the next little while!" She grins widely.
